parsed.explanation: The combined regime has no trans-specific criminal offence and no documented border exclusion, so it is not Severe Risk. But national restroom/biological-sex facility laws are universal-exposure measures reaching visitors, with no working remedy documented. Gender-identity anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage are not in force, public institutions are described as contributing to anti-LGBTIQ discrimination, and state framing treats trans facility use as a risk. A police torture conviction is positive but delayed and isolated; hate-crime data lack denominators. An adult alone faces facility exclusion and hostile interactions; a family with a minor faces bars on youth facility access. Overall: low-to-mid Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.interaction: Trans identity is not an offence, but no visitor-specific border or document practice is sourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No trans-specific offence or routine detention is documented. A historical police torture case against a trans activist shows custodial risk when police act.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: First sexual-discrimination torture conviction produced 17-year sentences, after nearly 20 years.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Remedies are slow and isolated; no visitor custody protocol is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National law bars restroom use by birth sex; the April 2025 sexual-integrity law bars trans people, including youth, from identity-matched facilities. Regional enforcement data are absent.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented; no working exemption or remedy is sourced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal facility exposure; may intensify hostile interactions, though no criminal penalty for restroom use is documented.

care_services.exposure: One regional hospital mistreatment complaint is pending; no visitor care denial is documented.
care_services.protection: Health guidance depathologised gender diversity; conversion therapy is banned for medical professionals; ministry says SOGI are not diseases.
care_services.interaction: These are largely resident-facing or climate signals; visitor care access is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Restroom law implicitly frames trans people as harassment risks; public institutions contribute to anti-LGBTIQ discrimination; no GI anti-discrimination or hate-crime coverage is in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts struck an anti-equality decree and permit legal gender change, but these are not documented visitor remedies.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing plus absent recourse raises the impact of being outed.

minors_guardians.exposure: April 2025 law bars trans youth from facilities matching identity; vague child-protection articles enable censorship. Equal age of consent is 14.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy is banned for medical professionals; education curriculum includes gender and sexuality information.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a minor adds facility exclusion and hostile framing; no guardian-specific remedy is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Hate crimes are reported rising, with trans women most affected, but the figure is a sub-registry without denominator, so magnitude is unresolved. A police torture case is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Convictions exist: 17 years for police torture; venue staff sentenced for denying trans women entry.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Remedies exist but are slow and isolated; no GI hate-crime law is in force.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No GI anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; foreign-funding law may be weaponised against queer organising; restroom enforcement is unclear.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have ruled an anti-equality decree unconstitutional; Constitutional Court permits marker change; conversion therapy ban.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are not shown to reach visitors or reverse facility exclusion.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has routine border denial and no effective remedy. This dossier documents no entry denial, so it is somewhat higher, but its national restroom ban is a universal facility exclusion with similarly thin recourse.

0.45-C uses identity portals, fines and short holds, with costly labour courts. This dossier is similar or slightly lower: it has a national facility ban and no GI anti-discrimination coverage, though no custodial penalty for restroom use is documented.

0.55-B involves extended border screening and refused admission with appeal delays. This dossier lacks documented border friction, but its universal restroom exclusion and absent GI recourse place it below 0.55-B.

0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention, written reasons and compensation. This dossier documents none of those visitor protections and adds a national facility ban, so it is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is mixed but not catastrophic. There is no trans-specific criminal offence, same-sex conduct is lawful, trans identity is not criminalised, and courts have sometimes protected equality and convicted torturers. Those positives are mostly climate signals or slow, isolated remedies. The visitor-facing exposure is the national birth-sex restroom and facility rule, which applies across the jurisdiction and has no documented working remedy. It is compounded by absent gender-identity anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage, institutional discrimination, and state framing of trans facility use as a risk. Hate-crime data cannot establish elevated magnitude without denominators. An adult visitor faces universal facility exclusion and possible hostile interactions; a visitor with a minor faces direct bars on youth facility access. The score remains in the Elevated Risk band.
